### Exercise 6: Understanding `map()`

Consider the code we used to request life expectancy for each year:

```{r}
#| eval: false

life_expectancy <-
  map(
    years,
    get_indicator,
    indicator = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"
  )
```

**(a)** What is the first argument, `years`, telling `map()`?

**(b)** What is the second argument, `get_indicator`, telling `map()`?

**(c)** Why do we pass `indicator = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"` separately?

**(d)** Recall that we defined our function as:

```{r}
#| eval: false

get_indicator <- function(year, indicator) {
  # ...
}
```

Why does it matter that `year` is the first argument of `get_indicator()` in the `map()` call above?

<!-- BEGIN PROFILE:r-teaching-guide -->
::: {.content-visible when-profile="r-teaching-guide"}

::: {.teaching-block}

::: {.teaching-block-header}
Teaching Note
:::

::: {.teaching-block-body}

🎯 **Learning Objective**

Students should:

- explain what the first two arguments of `map()` do;
- distinguish between the input that changes across calls and arguments that stay fixed;
- understand how `map()` passes values from its first argument into the function;
- connect the order of function arguments to how the `map()` call works.

✅ **Core Concepts to Highlight**

- The first argument to `map()` is the vector of values we want to work through.
- The second argument tells `map()` which function to apply.
- `map()` takes one value from `years` at a time and passes it to `get_indicator()`.
- The named argument `indicator = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"` stays fixed across every call.
- Because `year` is the first argument of `get_indicator()`, each value from `years` is passed to `year`.
- The call is therefore equivalent to repeatedly running `get_indicator()` with a different year and the same indicator.

💬 **Suggested In-Class Prompts**

- What would the first call made by `map()` look like?
- What would the second call look like?
- Which value changes from one call to the next?
- Which value stays fixed?
- If `indicator` were the first argument of `get_indicator()`, would this `map()` call still do what we want?

📌 **Common Misunderstandings**

- Thinking that `map()` passes the full `years` vector to `get_indicator()` in one call.
- Thinking that `indicator` is being mapped over as well.
- Thinking that the second argument to `map()` is another value rather than the function to apply.
- Missing that the values in `years` are passed to the first argument of `get_indicator()`.

:::

:::

:::

<!-- BEGIN PROFILE:r-solutions -->
::: {.content-visible when-profile="r-solutions" when-profile="r-teaching-guide"}

::: {.solution-block}

::: {.solution-block-header}
Solution
:::

::: {.solution-block-body}

(a)

`years` tells `map()` which values to work through. `map()` takes one year at a time from this vector.

(b)

`get_indicator` tells `map()` which function to apply to each value in `years`.

(c)

`indicator = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"` is passed separately because it stays the same across every call. We want to change the year while continuing to request the same indicator.

(d)

`map()` passes each value from `years` to the first argument of `get_indicator()`. Because `year` is the first argument, each value is used as the year in the API request.

For example, the first two calls made by `map()` are equivalent to:

```{r}
get_indicator(
  year = 1960,
  indicator = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"
)

get_indicator(
  year = 1965,
  indicator = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"
)
```

:::

:::
